correctness.rationale: A nonzero evaluation has a unique least-valuation nonzero term because the residues of all nonzero terms modulo N are distinct. Dividing out that term gives a factor in 1+pℤ_p, an N-th power by Hensel since p∤N. Hence no quotient can leave the listed power cosets. Each coset is approached by quotients of single-coordinate evaluations: the bases of the powers range over ℚ×, dense in ℚ_p×. The power subgroup contains 1+pℤ_p, so is open and closed in ℚ_p×; adjoining zero to the finite union gives a closed set in the full field, and zero is an actual value quotient. At 2 and odd degree all units are powers, giving the exact difference-cover criterion. At most r(r−1) ordered differences can be nonzero, so r≥q+1 for N=q²+q+1. Independently checked the Singer argument including characteristic three: the trace polynomial X+X^q+X^(q²) is nonzero and has degree below q³, so the trace takes a nonzero value. For any c≠0, multiplication by c is invertible, giving nondegeneracy of the trace pairing. Thus a nonidentity coset cannot stabilize the trace-zero plane (equal kernels would give proportional functionals). Its translate meets that plane in exactly one projective point, giving one ordered representation per nonzero difference. Coefficients 2^d realize the resulting q+1 distinct residues, with all variables essential. This verifies the exact closure and attained lower bound with no reliance on finite sampling.

claim_vs_prior_implication.reasoning: The positive witness alone is a short synthesis of known arguments; it is not a new construction of difference sets. The old uniform threshold does not imply the least achievable count. To establish the full result one must turn the separate valuation arguments into a necessary-and-sufficient criterion for arbitrary distinct residues and retain the unit cosets, including primes outside the stricter coprimality hypothesis. The lower bound then reduces to counting differences, and the exact family is obtained by matching it with Singer. value.rationale: The closure determines precisely which regions are missing in a non-dense quotient set, including unit-class obstructions that a density-only test with surjective unit powers cannot see. The exact odd-degree family separates the least attainable variable count (q+1, order √N) from the older universal sufficient count (order N), and gives coefficients realizing that gap for infinitely many exponents. The useful content is the sharp boundary for integral forms and the closure description, not recomputing Singer parameters.
residual_risks: The minimum is within the distinct-residue family only; repeated-residue forms could have different thresholds.
